join_order.notes: Single keyword id resolves to small (<100) set of mk rows; use precomputed CSR index keyed by keyword_id.
title is dense PK, direct array index by (t_id-1); also handle INT32_MIN sentinel.

join_order.probe: cast_info.person_id (for ci rows of surviving t_id via offsets_only index)
join_order.notes: Pre-scan name (4.17M rows) with parallel substring search; verify pos(Downey)<pos(Robert). Build flat_hash_set<int32_t>. Tiny set (<200) but use hash set for O(1) membership.

join_order.probe: cast_info via cast_info__movie_id offsets_only for each surviving t_id
join_order.notes: For each surviving t_id, scan ci.person_id range [off[t_id], off[t_id+1]); if any pid in set, emit (t_id, pid).

parallelism.notes: Only the 4.17M name scan is large enough to parallelize (partition by row range, per-thread local hash set, merge at end). The mk-driven outer loop is tiny (<100 t_ids), keep serial to avoid sync overhead.

aggregation_notes: MIN(k.keyword) is the literal 'marvel-cinematic-universe' (single fixed k.id) — emit as constant, no scan. MIN(n.name) tracked over matched person_ids via name.off/name.dat lookup. MIN(t.title) tracked over surviving t_ids via title.off/title.dat lookup.

memory_loads.movie_keyword__keyword_id rowids: mmap (~17.3 MB) — only touched for one keyword's range
memory_loads.cast_info.person_id: mmap (~138 MB) — only touched for surviving t_id ranges
memory_loads.name.off / name.dat: mmap; full scan for filter; spot lookups for MIN output
memory_loads.title.off / title.dat: mmap; spot lookups for MIN output

early_exit: If target_k_id not found in keyword scan: emit NULL row and exit.
If downey_robert_ids is empty after name scan: emit NULL row and exit.
If CSR range for target_k_id is empty: emit NULL row and exit.
